#1933. Emotional Mauricio Pochettino gets perfect sendoff in his US farewell... before boarding jet for new life as Manchester United manager

By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER

Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.

Christian Pulisic, Pochettino's brightest pupil over the last two seasons, rose to the occasion by scoring on a gravity-defying bicycle kick in the 25th minute and 18-year-old prospect Julian Hall followed in the 43rd with a goal of his own.

But for all of the excitement on the field – where Pochettino helped rebuild the American attack with a high-intensity style – all eyes were on the manager as he embraced his team one last time.

With the 2-0 win (8-0 aggregate), the USMNT now advances to the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, but that's no longer Pochettino's concern. Instead, former American fullback and current under-23 manager Steve Cherundolo is expected to take over on an interim basis, while Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one win in the English Premier League through 10 matches this season.

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino said after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'

Following the win, Pochettino was scheduled to fly from northern Kentucky to Manchester aboard a private plane chartered by his new club. The quick escape offered the chance to avoid major airlines following Friday's chaotic nationwide shutdown, and perhaps a few hours' sleep for a 54-year-old starting his new job on Wednesday at Carrington Training Centre.

Pochettino spent two years with the USMNT, helping to rebuild an attack around Pulisic

Pochettino hugs a staff member prior to the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match

Pochettino paces along a near-empty sideline after much of his staff left for Manchester

And Pochettino didn't plan on traveling alone.

Outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott were expected to join Pochettino aboard the flight to Manchester, where assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

The Argentine national is replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'

Mauricio Pochettino saying his final goodbyes to the USA fans as he's now gonna fly to Manchester immediately ❤️ pic.twitter.com/sCe8LCjpK5

Pulisic, perhaps Pochettino's brightest pupil, scored on a bicycle kick in the 25th minute

Pulisic celebrates his goal on Tuesday night in Cincinnati during the win over Haiti

Pochettino was expected to board a flight from northern Kentucky to Manchester after the win

Pochettino had been on something of a farewell tour in the US, where he embraced the local sports scene over his brief tenure. In between overseeing his final games with the USMNT, Pochettino was spotted at the Cincinnati Bengals' win over the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

The manager, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead before kickoff, where he mingled with Bengals special teamers such as kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow.

A night earlier, Pochettino guided the US to a 6-0 win over Haiti in Miami to give his team a safe cushion for his farewell on Tuesday in Cincinnati.

Pochettino broke down in tears as he announced his decision last week, while admitting he couldn't turn down the 'dream' job with Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino walks on the field after the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal

American fans give Pochettino a standing ovation in Cincinnati after his farewell match

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team's headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

'I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,' he said. 'It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

'I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

'Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

'In some part it's a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

United will pay the US Soccer Federation more than $13.2 million (£10m) in compensation for Pochettino and his backroom staff.

'I never said I wanted to go back in the Premier League,' Pochettino, a former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, told reporters last week. 'All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear.'

Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one EPL win

Mauricio Pochettino insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT

Pochettino put together a 23-12-2 record with the US, while 78 players earned caps for the US over his tenure. Remarkably, nine teenagers made their USMNT debuts for Pochettino, including Hall, who scored on Tuesday.

But the Americans failed to crack into the sport's upper echelon during Pochettino's brief tenure in the US. In his lone World Cup appearance with the team last summer, Pochettino guided the USMNT to the Round of 16, where the Americans fell to Belgium, 4-1.

That result was an improvement on 2018, when the US failed to qualify, but not on 2022, when then-coach Gregg Berhalter's similarly team fell short of the quarters with a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands.

Despite this, Pochettino's American players have remained largely supportive of his tenure, including Berhalter's son Sebastian, who said the outgoing coach helped him 'develop as a player and as a person.'

Prior to Tuesday's win, Pochettino thanked American fans for the support he received over his two years with the national team.

'Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the fans, for all the people that was supporting us in the last two years,' Pochettino said in a video posted on social media. 'Special, great memories of the World Cup and everything that we lived together. Always in my heart, always one of you. All the best and I wish everything good for the future.'

Potential candidates to replace Pochettino in the US include former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and some lesser-known candidates like Cherundolo, who now guides the United States U-23 team.

'For us to win, we need to be great at a lot of things, and we need someone who cares about youth development, cares about our youth national team programs, our relationships with our clubs and the success of the federation more broadly,' US Soccer CEO JT Batson told TNT Sports on Tuesday. 'We know that is a key part of our success, and it's also a key part of how we've been able to attract great people because they get to do big things.'

#1926. Pep Guardiola visits Bahia in new City Football Group role

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

Guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

The visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

"I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them."

Almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

During their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us."

Guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, New York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

His journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

The visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been announced, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

Nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would currently secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

For Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.

And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

Against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

After seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively Hayden Velvick restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

The hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

This time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of Noel Leighton. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

The home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

There was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely important result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

Bridges team: Roberts, Ferreira, J Hallard (Irving 75), Adeyinka, Neathey, Leighton (C), R Hallard (Dundas 65), Malone, Saunders, Velvick, Bennett (Idowu-Johnson 87)

Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki have both been left out of Manchester City’s starting lineup for this afternoon’s Premier League fixture against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.

The Citizens are seeking to bounce back from a run of three successive top-flight defeats, most recently losing 3-1 away against Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Manager Enzo Maresca has made a total of three changes to the side that were beaten at the City Ground, with Fernandez, Cherki and Josko Gvardiol all dropping down to the substitutes’ bench.

While Cherki scored in the defeat to Forest, Gvardiol was at fault for a first-half goal conceded by City and Fernandez’s position in midfield has come under question in recent weeks.

Ayyoub Bouaddi will start just his third Premier League game at the expense of Fernandez, while Phil Foden and Nico O'Reilly have been brought in for Cherki and Gvardiol respectively.

While Matheus Nunes missed out through injury, Abdukodir Khusanov has shaken off a knock to start at right-back, joining O'Reilly, Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias in a four-man defence protecting goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Bouaddi will links arms with Elliot Anderson in centre-midfield, with Foden set to operate in the number 10 role between wingers Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku.

Leading the line is goal machine Erling Haaland, who has scored eight goals in as many games against Fulham and is looking to net his 10th Premier League goal of the campaign this afternoon.

As for Fulham, head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has also made a total of three changes to the team that rescued a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United a fortnight ago.

Arbeloa has also opted to change his full-backs, with Kenny Tete and Ryan Sessegnon coming in for Timothy Castagne and Antonee Robinson. Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber retain their places at centre-back, though.

Man City academy graduates Shea Charles and Oscar Bobb both start against their former club, with the former to play alongside Sander Berge in midfield and the latter continuing on the right flank.

Bart Verbruggen - 6: He conceded five for the Dutch against the Germans during the international break and another two here. Neither of McBurnies were his fault to be fair.

Chema - 6: The young Spaniard does the basics well and was good for the most part. Ran out of gas in the later stages. He was booked for a foul on Coyle.

Diego Gomez - 7: Fizzed a delightful cross into the box on 13 minutes which somehow just eluded everyone. He also supplied the cross that saw Ayari rattled the bar. Should have scored on 51 when he flashed an angled effort wide of the far post. Replaced by Kadioglu on 80.

Yasin Ayari - 6: Saw his first-time sliding effort well saved by Tzolakis. He probably should have scored. Rattled the bar with a brilliant first time effort on 36 minutes. He got into the positions but just not ruthless enough. Replaced by Hinshelwood on 66 minutes.

Max De Cuyper - 6: Delivered an accurate cross to tee-up Ayari's big chance on 14 minutes. Lacked the cutting edge needed to breakthrough this stubborn Hull team.

Georginio - 6: Selected ahead of Kostoulas and forced a sharp save from Tzolakis on 31 minutes with crisp right footed effort. Tzolakis then denied him on 38 minutes with an even better save. #1919. You're Not Nineteenth Forever! Sacked Man United manager Michael Carrick looks relieved to be out of the relegation fight as he watches The Courteeners at gig in London

Published: 04:29 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend (Source X/adamkearey)

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

Some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

United are back in action on Sunday when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool in what will be Pochettino's first game in charge.

Hurzeler added: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards. In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon a frustrating game but we have to keep going.

"We will analyse it. That's the process we follow. I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time."

Brighton, for the first time this season, seemed to run out of gas in the closing stages and the the Costinha sending off tipped the balance in Hull’s favour.

Hurzeler said: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role. We made a decision, at that moment, a wrong decision, but we will analyse it.

“My team was desperate to win it, of course, in certain elements be more patient, be more disciplined, be more structured.

“That's what we missed, not only in the last minutes, also in the minutes before, and again, we will analyse it and make it better.”

#1916. New heights and same problems: How Milan stars fared in the November international break

With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about…

Christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s quickly reminded everyone of how important he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

It gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

In terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

However, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence currently and long may it continue.

Then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

He played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

For France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

For Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

It was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

#1915. I watched Celtic beat St Mirren and spotted unexpected renaissance, O’Neill’s remedy and mystery man

Celtic made light work of St Mirren at the weekend as they ran out 4-1 winners on Saturday afternoon to maintain their lead at the Scottish Premiership.

Three goals in nine first-half minutes from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (33), Camilo Duran (40) and Luke McCowan (42) put the hosts on course for a comfortable victory, before captain Callum McGregor added to the scoreline in the second period (63). A Killian Phillips penalty (69) provided a consolation for the visitors.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The win keeps Celtic four points clear at the top of the table after second-placed Rangers won 2-1 at Motherwell later in the evening kick-off. But what did their win over St Mirren tell us about Celtic’s hopes of winning a sixth successive league title come May?

Graham Falk was at Parkhead to cover proceedings. These are his three key takeaways from Celtic’s win vs St Mirren:

Mika Baur’s injury looks like it may rule him out for up to 10 weeks and is clearly a big blow for Celtic. The young German has been one of their most impressive performers this season. With Benjamin Nygren also absent, Luke McCowan was handed his first start since September 20.

Forced to delete his social media account to escape personal abuse from sections of the online support just a few short weeks ago, it would have been hard to blame McCowan had he sunk into his shell when an audible groan greeted one of his early misplaced passes at Parkhead. But to McCowan’s credit, he did quite the opposite, and scored Celtic’s clinching third goal just before half-time.

Of course, one swallow doesn’t make a summer, but it’ll take a major weight off his shoulders, and could benefit Celtic with Baur out for a while. The ex-Dundee skipper will admit himself that he’s not been at the level expected this season. But, as proven by his 23 goal contributions across Celtic’s last two title-winning seasons, he’s shown previously that he can play an important role.

He’ll never be viewed as someone who will take Celtic to the next level, but he can take confidence from his performance and give O’Neill a valuable option as he awaits Nygren and Baur’s return to full fitness.

In his previous stint as Celtic manager, the veteran boss loved to play with a front two. However, more out of necessity, he’s almost exclusively opted for a front three over the last 12 months. Previous managers Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers both moulded their side that way, and O’Neill has stuck with it. It’s had its doubters, though, with some calling for him to partner Kasper Hogh with Duran, rather than shifting the Colombian out on the wing to accommodate him.

But did the front three that started against St Mirren show a way forward for O’Neill? Starting Jota and Yang either side of Duran for the first time, the trio were a constant threat throughout for Celtic, who looked a more free-flowing outfit offensively than they have for several weeks.

“Yang is something else for us at the moment,” said O’Neill post-match. “Duran is a top, top quality centre-forward, and Jota is still trying to get up to the speed of the game. But Yang is so strong, he made the first goal for us, and what he does for us defensively is just amazing when you consider he is a wide player.”

It was the main question before, during and after the game, in the stands and in the press room. The mystery surrounding Haissem Hassan. Where was he? One of Celtic’s big summer signings, he was left out of the matchday squad for the second successive game, putting the rumours into overdrive.

Ahead of the game, O’Neill had quashed suggestions that the Egyptian was omitted from the squad for their last game because he was ‘unpopular’ with other members of his Celtic squad. However, his absence against St Mirren at the weekend was simply due to “rotation”. Hmm.

They didn’t miss him too much on the field, with Celtic rolling to a comfortable win over their Paisley counterparts. However, while no one can say Duran hasn’t repaid the £6million fee shelled out on him, the combined £20million spent on Hogh and Hassan is rightly being brought into question. We’re almost into December: one can’t get into the squad, and the other hasn’t scored a goal in over 1000 minutes. Surely O’Neill expected much more bang for his buck, even if he won’t admit it publicly.

For the Rocks, Henry Nevill hooked a cross in from the left but Callum Laycock looped it up into the air with his head. Lennie Smith sped down the right but his cross-shot was saved.

Bognor extended their lead on 25 minutes when Roberts' shot was pushed out only as far as McDonald, who diverted it into the net on the rebound, despite Forster getting something on it.

From McDonald's corner, Tommy Block was denied in a crowded penalty area. On 38 minutes Joshua Edwards had to receive treatment as he took a bash to the head in a challenge with Laycock.

Smith got on the breakaway for Bognor and he fed McDonald, who struck a shot wide along the deck. Harry Grant blasted over as Hayes were very wasteful in front of goal.

Four minutes after the break, a fierce ball in from Dernell Wynter saw Ferdinand divert it in from close range to make it 2-1.

Shroll got another dangerous ball into the box but Amos Nasha's header was directed straight at Tommy Scott. Shroll went into the book for a shoulder barge into the back of Smith. Kaya Tshaka's free-kick picked out Block but his header was saved.

Tshaka swiped at a chance of his own and he had to come off injured. Ethan Robb replaced him.

Nevill blazed a cross from the left too high before Fashanu hit a curling effort with his right foot and Scott palmed it out. Fashanu hit a corner deep towards the back post with Shroll under it, but Laycock and Scott combined to keep it out.

Nasha did well to pass the ball to Ferdinand and he hit the right post with his low effort on 69 minutes. Roberts was replaced by Ben Anderson for the Rocks and Nasha went into the book as he pulled Nevill back.

Scott pulled out a wonderful save down to his right to keep Grant’s low volleyed effort from just outside the area. Ferdinand was offside on the rebound.

Ollie Lovell came off on 80 minutes for Bognor, then the referee pulled up injured with a strained calf so Bognor's public address announcer, Peter Kelly-Sullivan, had to take up the flag for linesman’s duty for the remainder of the game.

Brendan Matthew had a header diverted wide when he had the goal at his mercy in the 94th minute.

It was a nervy final moments for the Rocks with the visitors always a danger but they held on for the win.

Next up is the highly-anticipated game away to Jersey Bulls – and over 200 Bognor fans are expected to make the trip to the island on Saturday.

#1913. I watched Rangers down Motherwell and spotted Ibrox’s new leading man, injury blow plus eyebrow-raising stat

Rangers maintained their strong run of domestic form by defeating Motherwell 2-1 at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez had his headed opener for the away side cancelled out by a Jake Girdwood-Reich effort before Ryan Naderi’s deflected winner. It means Rangers are second and four points behind Premiership leaders Celtic with a game in hand while Motherwell sit 10th after their latest defeat.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

I was at the game played in bitterly cold North Lanarkshire conditions. Here are some of the things I spotted.

Whisper it in hushed tones... but this is the type of game that teams who go on to clinch silverware usually grind out. The expected goals tally of both sides show the tale of the tape, where not too dissimilar to Rangers’ 1-0 at Ibrox last time out, Derek McInnes’ side battered on the door without getting through.

Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was doing his best ‘you shall not pass’ Gandalf impression, but much like The Balrog dragging the grey wizard from Lord of the Rings into the abyss, eventually his resistance was broken. It was messy but Rangers cared not as they got their winner just before a minimal amount of stoppage time was added on. It’s a clash teams of the recent past in Govan coughed points up in and making it 13 unbeaten domestically will be of great satisfaction to boss McInnes.

Motherwell under Alfred Johansson have set their stall out as a side who want to dominate the ball but that hasn’t happened in either home game against Rangers or Celtic. Both sides of the Old Firm have come to Fir Park and been able to dictate play, Martin O’Neill’s side winning 2-0 last month, having controlled proceedings with well over 60% possession. This was much the same albeit the Fir Park defence stood valiantly until they were eventually overwhelmed, Rangers enjoying just under that 60% mark in terms of time on the ball.

Motherwell fans, and supporters of other provincial clubs, have been used to these types of games against Glasgow’s big two over the years. It’s a defensive stand that more often than not ends in defeat, but it’s more of a shock to the system for Motherwell, given what they have built over the last 18 months. Rangers’ winner was perhaps harsh with the effort put in but the amount of chances coughed up proved there could be little complaints over their visitors claiming all three points. Key playmaker Ibrahim Said looked visibly emotional after being subbed in the first half with injury and that will be of major concern to boss Johansson, with much of his side’s good attacking play usually involving the Nigerian.

Since replacing an injured Lawrence Shankland last time out versus Motherwell, Ryan Naderi has been a man transformed. He bundled home the winner off defender Martin Moormann here to make it 11 goal contributions in as many games. Questions over quality were abundant last term upon his arrival from Hansa Rostock but he has been vital for McInnes this term.

Amid long-term blows to Shankland and Youssef Chermiti, Naderi has firmly made himself Rangers’ main man in attack. Any striker coming into the team would need to play alongside him as it’s hard to see how they function without him. It might be unconventional at times but Naderi’s pressing and knack of being in the right place at the right time is proving invaluable.

This clash between Motherwell and Rangers was the first time since Opta records began in season 2005/06 that there was not one Scottish player in the starting line-up of a top-flight match. As conversations continue over development of young talent in our country, it’s perhaps inevitable it became a talking point across analysis of the match.

Let’s get off our high horses for a minute though as the conversation with this particular game needs more nuance. Alex Lowry and Stephen O’Donnell are regular starters for Motherwell but both were unavailable, while club captain Paul McGinn is only recently back from long-term injury. James Penrice would likely have been a starter for Rangers had he been fully fit while Findlay Curtis did get on to make a key impact in the winner. Callum Hendry offered more bite to the home attack at the other end. All of that is not to say a lack of development Scottish talent isn’t an issue, it is, but perhaps this stat isn’t the platform to build that argument from.

#1911. Chelsea news: Mykhaylo Mudryk continues Andriy Shevchenko war of words, accuses Ukrainian legend of lying

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 11:25

Chelsea winger Mykhaylo Mudryk has continued his war of words with UAF president Andriy Shevchenko over the circumstances surrounding his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, currently on loan at Tottenham Hotspur, was given the green light to return to football in July 2026 after serving a ban of more than 18 months for testing positive for meldonium.

However, the winger did an interview earlier this week that reopened the saga, with the 25-year-old claiming that the drug could have only entered his system while on international duty with Ukraine.

Shevchenko, a former Chelsea striker and Ukraine legend, hit back at those suggestions, alleging that Mudryk wanted a UAF employee to take responsibility for his ban.

He went as far as calling for Mudryk to retract his claims against the UAF and the Ukraine national team. Instead, Mudryk has since doubled-downed on his initial comments.

As quoted by BBC Sport, a statement read: "Neither I nor my representatives made any such request.

"My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible.

"In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. One of those letters was leaked to the media by the UAF earlier today and clearly shows that my lawyers wanted 'true, verifiable and reliable information.

"Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case.

"For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. That is, I have evidence to prove that their repeated assertions are wrong."

Despite his previous status as Ukraine's best player, it feels unlikely that Mudryk will represent his country anytime soon.

There have been two opportunities for either Mudryk or Shevchenko to back down, but it is clear that both parties remain firm over their stance.

Mudryk is currently pushing to return from injury to feature for Spurs, his solitary appearance for the North Londoners having come in September.

#1910. Rangers have discovered steely edge as late Fir Park drama offers glimpse of growing title-winning mentality

There was no disguising the satisfaction in Tuur Rommens' voice as he reflected on Rangers' late 2-1 victory over Motherwell. It provided the Belgian defender with further evidence of a team learning learning how to grind out results and develop a winning mentality to overcome hurdles when it matters most.

Rangers looked in danger of leaving Fir Park frustrated on Saturday night after a performance in which their attacking intent was not always matched by clinical finishing. Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen had done everything within his power to earn his side a point, producing a string of outstanding saves, but Rangers refused to settle for a draw.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Their persistence was eventually rewarded in the 88th minute when Ryan Naderi’s effort took a deflection off Martin Moorman, wrong-footing Paulsen and finding the net. Those heroics sparked jubilant celebrations among the sizeable travelling support.

Rommens acknowledged that such a dramatic conclusion in North Lanarkshire could provide a significant boost to morale inside the away dressing room, praising his team-mates' willingness to keep pushing despite facing a goalkeeper in inspired form.

“The spirit was good and especially when you score a goal in the last minute of the game, it always gives an extra boost,” said the left-back. “Everybody was very happy in the dressing room. It's never easy to come here and to win. Last year we didn't win here, so it's nice to come here and win and get the three points.

“We had a lot of chances. The finish was not always there, but we played a very good game. It feels like we've gained these two points. Their goalkeeper did an amazing job. It's not only our finishing, it's also credit that he saves a lot of shots. Of course, if it stays 1-1, you're thinking, ‘oh, come on, we need to get another one’. But at the end, we got what we deserved.”

Rangers were left to rue too many dropped points last season, and Rommens is acutely aware of how big the difference between settling for a point and claiming all three can be over the course of a campaign.

The connection between the players and supporters is another factor the 23-year-old believes is proving invaluable in helping Rangers navigate difficult moments.

“The fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn't feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us,” he added. “When you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they're so happy, we're so happy, so it gives us an extra boost to go again on Tuesday and try to get another win.”

Attention now turns to Rangers’ game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, with Derek McInnes’ side looking to capitalise on a run of three successive home fixtures and build on their 13-game unbeaten streak.

The bigger picture remains firmly in their sights, although Rommens is not interested in becoming distracted by the current state of the title race.

“It's been a long time (since we last played at Ibrox). So it will be nice to play in front of our fans again,” he said. “I think at home we have to maintain our good run. You just need to keep winning and at the end you'll see where you're at. But if you keep winning, you'll be up there.”

#1909. Five alive: Bexhill move on up with win over Midhurst

Since Bexhill secured a win in the reverse fixture in September, Midhurst have struggled to recover from internal strife that saw their manager and a number of players depart, with a run of poor results that has plunged them into the relegation mire.

Meanwhile, Bexhill have managed to strike a rich vein of form with a squad that blends youth with experience and a strong sense of togetherness and solidarity.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Missing Luke Donaldson with a three-match ban, Pirates gaffer Jay Skinner-Swain kept Ash Latuske and Ryan Moir in their attacking positions on the flanks with Charlie Scarles slotting into an advanced role in midfield.

Bexhill couldn’t have hoped for a better start. In the first minute Theo Coombs had a chance well saved but from the resulting corner Charlie Playford ghosted into the six yard box to beat all-comers with a bullet header from point blank range.

Three minutes later Latuske beat two men with a powerful run down the right to set up Shonk and the Bexhill record goalscorer made no mistake in adding another to his tally.

It looked like Bexhill would run amok but it’s all credit to the young Midhurst lads that they didn’t just fold. They put in some decent enough approach moves but the Pirates defence had the measure of them.

At the other end, another goal looked almost inevitable. On 25 minutes Shonk had an effort cleared off the line from a Moir corner. Shortly after, Scarles had an effort well saved by the young Midhurst keeper who was keeping his side in with a sniff.

Just before the break there was nothing he could do though as Latuske lashed in a drive that had the keeper beaten all ends up but the ball somehow bounced back out into play off the inside of the post.

Bexhill went in two goals to the good at half-time but on the balance of play and chances it should have been more.

Almost inevitably Midhurst delivered a scare early in the second half. Just five minutes in, a runner skipped past the Bexhill defensive lines and delivered a ball which was swept into the Pirates net. It was followed minutes later by a good effort that required a fine save from Finn Holter.

But the moment soon passed for Midhurst and Bexhill got back in amongst it. The killer goal came on 55 and it was that man Coombs again, benefitting from some more great play from Latuske and swivelling to tuck the chance away.

Now it really was all Bexhill as Midhurst wilted under the pressure. On 65 minutes Latuske was at it again, this time setting up Shonk, whose shot curled just wide of the post. It was the briefest of respites for Midhurst as Moir played in Coombs on the left and this time he turned provider, chipping in a perfect cross for Shonk to nod home for 4-1.

Bexhill were rampant now and on 76 minutes substitute Jack Samways wrapped it up at 5-1 to the Pirates with the pick of the afternoon’s goals. Winning the ball just inside the box he crashed a perfect half volley into the Brockley Road End net.

It was no less than Bexhill deserved for a thoroughly professional demolition job on their hapless visitors.

The Pirates move up sixth in the league and have a chance to keep their current run going with the long trip over to Pagham on Saturday afternoon.

#1908. Pavlovic admits he liked Conceicao despite ‘Hitler-like’ methods: “Such a circus”

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has admitted that he was a fan of Sergio Conceicao, even if his management was rather totalitarian.

It’s fair to say that Conceicao is a divisive figure within the Milan sphere. The Portuguese arrived and won the Supercoppa Italiana and there were glimpses of the Rossoneri becoming a team under him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, there were far too many incidents which turned most against him – including some members of the squad – and that gave him little hope of continuing. So, when he lost the Coppa Italia against Bologna, he was all but done, if he wasn’t before then.

He’s called it unfair since, but logically there was no way he could’ve continued.

Speaking to the Serbian podcast SS Calcio, Pavlovic admitted that he was fond of Conceicao, despite some of his strange methods, as MilanNews relays.

“Conceicao banned Nutella, and since then they haven’t allowed it [he laughs]. He was… He’s a good guy, I like him, but he had Hitler-like methods. We go away for a match and at the hotel we split up; the players stay together, everyone else stays outside.

“Knee and elbow pads are mandatory in training, whether the temperatures are below zero or 35 degrees; they have to be there.

“Three days before a match, some players went to a concert until 11 p.m.… He had assistants, or spies if you like, who reported to him, and he made such a circus out of it that in the next match, none of those five or six players were allowed on the pitch.”

Another anecdote about Conceiçao, when he had just been appointed coach of Milan…

“He was 40 minutes late to the first meeting; all the players and management were waiting for him, and he was in his office. He just wanted everyone to know who was in charge. He did it on purpose.”

It’s certainly a strong comparison to make; that’s for sure…

#1905. Fabian Hurzeler reveals what frustrated him most about Brighton's defeat at Hull

The Seagulls looked on course for at least a point at the MKM Stadium, before two stoppage-time goals from Oli McBurnie condemned them to defeat.

Hurzeler – who was booked by the referee late on in the match – felt Brighton had been the better side for much of the contest. But he criticised their performance after the opening 65 minutes, admitting they had allowed Hull back into the game.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking to Match of the Day, he said: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we chopped our intensity, levels and standards.

"In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going."

Brighton were reduced to ten men in the 89th minute, when Costinha received a second yellow card for pushing Sorba Thomas to the ground.

McBurnie then struck in the 92nd and 95th minutes to secure all three points for Hull.

Asked whether the dismissal had contributed to the late goals, Hurzeler said: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role."

The Brighton boss also acknowledged the outstanding performance of Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who made several important saves to keep his side in the game.

"We have to give credit to him. He made a good performance but in the end it's our responsibility," Hurzeler said.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Hurzeler described Hull's opening goal as a ‘lucky punch’ but insisted Brighton had to take responsibility for the result.

"That's football. The Premier League is ruthless. Hull scored with a lucky punch, we have to accept it and be better next time.”

He suggested his players had become impatient as they struggled to make their chances count.

"We rushed things, we lost a bit of intensity, we tried to force things because we weren't patient enough," he said.

"For 65 minutes we could easily win the game.

"You can easily get frustrated if you miss so many chances."

Hurzeler was also full of praise for Tzolakis, describing him as a ‘great goalkeeper’ who had produced a ‘big performance’.

The Brighton manager was asked about a penalty appeal involving Pascal Gross but said he had not watched the incident back.

"The referee wasn't the reason why we lost today.”

Hurzeler insisted his team would analyse what went wrong but stressed the importance of maintaining their standards in the Premier League.

"We will analyse it – that's the process we follow," he told Match of the Day.

"I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time."

#1903. Tottenham eye £22m move for Ligue 2 goal machine

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 12:05, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 12:06

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly tracking one of French football's most prolific young players, but could face a significant financial obstacle and an unusual transfer arrangement if they pursue a January deal.

Roberto De Zerbi's side have identified Stade de Reims midfielder Yaya Fofana as a potential target, with scouts expected to attend Saturday's Ligue 2 encounter against Saint-Etienne to assess the 22-year-old in person.

According to Foot Mercato, Tottenham are impressed by the Ivory Coast international's remarkable start to the season. However, Reims are unwilling to lose their leading attacking performer midway through their promotion campaign and would reportedly demand more than €25m (£22m).

The French club could nevertheless consider a deal allowing Fofana to remain on loan until the summer, potentially enabling interested teams to secure his signature without immediately removing him from Nicolas Usai's squad.

Fofana's emergence is particularly striking given that he spent more than a year on the sidelines between 2025 and 2026 after suffering a serious stress fracture.

The former Lens youngster has returned in outstanding form, benefiting from Usai's decision to deploy him further forward. Although naturally a midfielder capable of operating in defensive and central positions, he has developed into Reims' principal attacking threat.

Fofana has scored 11 goals and provided two assists in 12 Ligue 2 appearances, placing him at the top of the division's goalscoring charts despite not being a conventional centre-forward.

His finishing efficiency is equally remarkable. Of his 19 shots on target, 11 have resulted in goals, while his tally considerably exceeds his expected-goals figure of 4.9. That represents an overperformance of 6.1 goals, although maintaining such clinical finishing throughout the campaign would be difficult.

Earlier this month, Fofana also received his first Ivory Coast call-up, marking another significant milestone following his lengthy injury absence.

Tottenham reportedly admire his versatility and attacking output, while Foot Mercato claims that the player is attracted by the prospect of competing in England. Saturday's encounter with Ligue 2 leaders Saint-Etienne offers Spurs' scouts an opportunity to assess him against strong opposition.

Despite the growing interest, Reims are determined to retain Fofana for the remainder of their promotion campaign.

According to Foot Mercato, the French club would not accept less than the €25m (£22m) received from Patrick Zabi's recent sale, with Fofana's performances strengthening their negotiating position.

An immediate January departure is reportedly off the table, although a transfer followed by a six-month loan back to Reims could provide a compromise. Tottenham would secure a long-term investment, while the French side would retain a crucial player for the decisive months of the season.

Competition could complicate matters. Galatasaray have also been linked with Fofana, while Stuttgart and Trabzonspor are reportedly monitoring his progress.

Reims' negotiating position is strengthened by the midfielder's long-term contract. Several reports list its expiry as June 2030, although the club's most recent publicly confirmed extension, announced in November 2024, ran until June 2029.

For Tottenham, scouting remains the expected next step. No offer has been confirmed, and there is no indication of an agreement with Reims or the player.

Fofana's impressive performances have made him one of Ligue 2's standout players, but Reims' insistence on keeping him until the summer means that any interested club must decide whether securing an early agreement justifies an investment exceeding £22m.

Published: 05:52 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 05:53 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata announced the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq

Juan Mata has announced his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata)

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with plans to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

‘When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It’s probably been the summer or the transfer window where there’s been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

‘And we’ve said publicly and we’ve said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

‘And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we’re receiving a lot of criticism for it but we’re actually happy with the players that we bought.

‘It’s true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

‘When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.’

Berrada also addressed United’s decision not to sign a new left-sided defender after the club made an enquiry for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

‘When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there’s a lot of discussion about the back line,’ Berrada said.

‘But we did come into it thinking we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

‘So that’s why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it’s been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

‘I think what we’ve seen in the back line is we’ve had injuries, it’s taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back. Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

‘So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

‘There’s no point in us spending £40 million, £50m for players that we’re not convinced are going to add value to the team.

‘So it’s always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward.

‘When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don’t necessarily add quality to the team.

‘Because when you sign a player that doesn’t work out for Man Utd, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

‘So when I talk about being disciplined, I’m not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players. We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent. So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don’t want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it.’

#1895. Newcastle vs. Arsenal: Why Mikel Arteta should fear "hellish" St James' Park return

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 12:28

Ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Arsenal, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton warns Mikel Arteta to expect a "horrible" evening at St James' Park.

Newcastle vs. Arsenal is just always one of those really awkward fixtures. The only two modern wins I can remember in the current decade were towards the end of the 2022-23 season and of course last season, that magnificent Merino and Gabriel comeback.

Apart from that, St. James' Park has been a pretty hellish ground for Arsenal. But the stats do not lie this season.

Five points clear at the top, nine wins from 10. Only four teams have had a better start than Arsenal's 27 points from 30: Chelsea in 2005-06, City in 2011-12, City in 2017-18, and Liverpool in 2019-20.

All four of those teams went on to win the title.

By that logic, I think this is Arsenal's title to lose, though perhaps too early to say that definitively.

Arsenal fans should be overwhelmingly happy, but there is always that sense we want more. So many of the wins have been narrow, one-nil victories. The Nottingham Forest win needed a deflected goal. The Hull win needed a rebound.

Hull set up in that 5-4-1 deep block, and Arsenal got a little fortuitous, but they also did not get a penalty that the key match incidents panel later said we should have had.

I was also frustrated at Noni Madueke for spurning that late one-on-one chance. He got caught in two minds going around the goalkeeper, when he should have tried to curl it into the bottom corner.

He was clearly upset with himself afterwards. That said, I do not want to be too critical of Madueke right now, because with Dowman still out suspended, Saka still out injured, Madueke has come to the fore in recent weeks.

He has not hit those same numbers that Saka was putting up a couple of years ago at his peak, but many aspects of his game have come on significantly.

He will start on the right-hand side here, and the Madueke versus Lewis Hall battle will be a fascinating one to watch.

But above all else, Arsenal just need to start blowing teams away. Arteta said as much after the Hull City win. He now has 34 1-0 wins in the Premier League since taking charge, the most of any manager in that period.

Arsenal have only scored five goals in their five away games, so I would not be surprised to see another 1-0 here. I am confident for an Arsenal win, but at St. James' Park there is always that hint of fear.

Under the lights, if the team and the fans get going, it can be a horrible place to visit as an Arsenal fan.

His successor, Dave Challinor, is miles from his destination but even if it might have been premature after two league games, "Wednesday are back" was a vote of confidence he can guide them to the right path.

The Owls did not play at anywhere near the level of the team they aspire to be. Jamal Lowe's goals were their only shots on target.

Much has been made of the entertainment levels this season, but a night so cold you could see every breath in a derby mismatched enough that you felt the Owls had much more to lose than gain was not about putting on a show, just coming back into the warm three points better off.

Barry Bannan ran around like a man ten years younger, Liam Cooper marshalled his defence, Lowe played in a wide position that demands a lot of dirty work without forgetting his primary job.

Barnsley refused to accept their fate when Lowe scored his second goal after 14 minutes.

The trouble is, like Wednesday's players last season, they are just not good enough for the level. Between the boxes they are, but not the bits that decide matches.

Their defending for Lowe's goals – leaving Cooper unmarked at a Bannan corner to head across to Lowe, then standing off the striker as he finished a move which took them from the halfway line to the back of the net in two passes and a shot – was relegation standard.

With the exception of Vimal Yoganathan arriving onto Reyes Cleary's low ball in to halve the deficit after 40 minutes, their final balls and finishes were not much better.

That they are trying their best only highlights their best is not good enough – not by much in most games, but by enough in almost all of them. Their winless run in League One now stretches to double figures – unlike their points tally.

Bromley's win at Reading on Saturday sent them bottom of the table.

It is hard to see them escaping relegation without a really good January transfer window, and very hard to imagine even a quite good one.

"When you play games like Sheffield or Stockport or Oxford. Luton, you do not have the feeling the gap is too so big," said Stendel after 90 minutes which backed him up.

"Between both boxes, we are surely a team who shouldn't be in the bottom of the league, but games decided not between the boxes.

"You would think, 'What you do in training?' but (on Thursday) we prepared the team especially for a situation like (the second goal)."

Whilst adamant his team can pull things around, Patrick Kelly – standing in for the suspended Cameron McGeehan as captain – was not pulling any punches.

"You can't start games like that," he said. "We just had too many times this season where we just gave ourselves too much to do.

"We've conceded far too many from free-kicks and stuff.

"After that we were good, probably the better team for the rest of the game, but didn't create enough clear-cut chances."

Barnsley's doom and gloom was in contrast to the joy of away fans who made up about a third of the crowd condensed into one end.

It felt important they shared it with the players at full-time.

"They have to enjoy it and look forward to the next one," said Challinor. "It's probably a little bit outside my comfort zone (celebrating).

"It's brilliant to be able to celebrate, but more brilliant to be able to send them home happy. They've been through the mill over the past couple of years, and maybe there's a little bit of a feeling they've got the they've got the football club back.

"You build that camaraderie between the team and supporters by winning and we've done that on the last couple of couple of occasions.

"We need to improve individually, collectively. There's so much more to come.

"But most importantly for the supporters, they want to see effort. They want to see the team put the bodies on the line. They did that in the second half."

After too much darkness, they think they can see the light. Barnsley fans are squinting to make it out.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard (Santos 86), Cooper, Swinkels (Palmer 70); Heskey, Mitchell (Barry 70), Slattery, Bannan (Gray 78), J Lowe (Liongola 70); Keillor-Dunn.

#1893. GdS: A red-hot start and the ‘S’ word – the data that inspires confidence in Amorim

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

It is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

To date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the new era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target announced by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

In short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

Conte was among the names initially explored along with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. The Italian, a free agent since parting ways with Napoli, was thought to be keen on the role at Old Trafford but it was widely reported United had reservations over some of his methods.

#1891. Harry Kane injury: Bayern Munich and England striker facing ‘months’ out

Harry Kane is facing several months out after suffering an ankle ligament injury during Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga game on Friday night.

The England captain was forced off after just 20 minutes following a challenge from defender Joel Schmied during Bayern’s 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old, who won the Ballon d’Or last month, initially tried to carry on before he limped off the pitch alongside Bayern’s medical staff.

Bayern issued an update after the game which read: ‘Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Koln on Friday evening.

‘This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.’

Bayern have seven more fixtures until their winter break in December. The German champions resume their Bundesliga campaign on January 9 and are also due to play Manchester United in the Champions League on January 20.

‘We have to do it without Harry, we have to do it without these guys,’ said Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany.

‘They are world-class players. You can’t replace them. But we have the mentality and we have to bring that.’
